exposure: modified World Health Organization (mWHO) group classification of heart disease severity
outcome: maternal major cardiac events (MACEs) (including maternal death, pulmonary edema, acute heart failure, endocarditis, stroke, myocardial infarction, acute aortic syndromes, arrhythmias requiring urgent treatment, and urgent intervention)
obstetric events (including HELLP syndrome, preeclampsia, eclampsia, placental abruption, obstetric hemorrhage)
cohort: A cohort of 399 pregnant women with heart disease from two referral centers in Mexico City who had deliveries between March 2014 and March 2019.
finding: Maternal major cardiac events (MACEs) and preterm birth were significantly associated with the severity of heart disease as classified by mWHO groups (mWHO II, II-III, III, and IV), while obstetric events were not associated with heart disease severity.
